items.title: Financial Support Today, Self-Reliance Tomorrow
items.summary: Manikala Durga’s Journey towards Economic Self-Reliance 07 OCT 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi Timely support for livelihood activities can provide opportunities to enhance income, strengthen family financial security and promote greater dignity and self-reliance.

facts.text: Ms. Manikala Durga, aged 39, belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community and has been working as a waste picker in the Guntur Municipal Corporation for the past 15 years.
Before receiving assistance, her livelihood depended primarily on waste-picking activities, through which she earned approximately Rs. 8,000 per month.
The group project had a total project cost of Rs. 35,03,500, comprising a loan of Rs. 21,27,624 and a capital subsidy of Rs. 13,75,876.

With the effective utilisation of the financial assistance, Ms. Durga has been able to generate an additional income of approximately Rs. 8,000 per month, taking her total monthly income to around Rs. 16,000.

bullets: Art. 340: the President appoints a commission on socially and educationally backward classes (APP).
The Constitution does not define "backward classes" (G2 2017 key: that was the incorrect statement). Art. 16(4) backward classes are mainly identified by caste/social backwardness (Indra Sawhney).

Before 2018, Art. 338(10) treated references to SCs as including such backward classes as the President specified - hence BC complaints went to the SC commission ; the 102nd Amendment added Art. 366(26C) defining SEBCs by reference to Art. 342A .

bullets: State average rainfall ~966 mm; Rayalaseema and south coast depend more on the NE monsoon.
Retreating monsoon: withdraws October-November; Bay of Bengal cyclones bring the rain of this season to the southern states.
SW monsoon (June-September) gives ~2/3 (65-70%) of AP's rainfall. It sets in during the 2nd week of June; July is the wettest month (CDI; APP).
Normal rainfall (APSES 2024-25): SWM 574.7 mm + NEM 285.3 mm = ~860 mm a year. CDI prints a State average of ~966 mm (older figure). 2024: SWM 681.6 mm (+18.6%); NEM 278.7 mm (-2.3%).

bullets: RBI Governor: How Chairperson (ex officio); casting vote on a tie
One RBI officer: How Nominated by the RBI Central Board
A statutory body under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, created by the 2016 amendment. It fixes the policy repo rate needed to hit the inflation target, and its decisions bind RBI.
Each member has one vote and decisions are by majority. The Governor has a casting vote in a tie. The MPC must meet at least 4 times a year; in practice it meets bi-monthly (six times).

Latest decisions: on 5 Aug 2026 the MPC voted unanimously to hold the repo at 5.25% with a neutral stance (TH, 6 Aug 2026). The minutes of the August meeting point to a likely hike: headline inflation averaged 3.93% so far this year and core inflation is projected at 4.3% for 2026-27 (TH, 20 Aug 2026).

bullets: Market intervention (spot and forward), forex reserves, forex swaps, monetary policy signalling (hawkish stance / repo hike attracts carry-trade capital); fiscal policy is not an RBI tool.

NDF curbs: offshore Non-Deliverable Forward market (Singapore/London) used to short the rupee - RBI restricts domestic banks' offshore NDF participation and enforces Net Open Position limits; in Apr 2026 RBI moved on Non-Deliverable Derivative (NDD) contracts to curb volatility (LENS Apr 2026).

Interest-rate signal: Example repo 5.25%, unchanged for the 4th meeting (Aug 2026)
Not an RBI exchange-rate tool: fiscal policy adjustments (APPSC-G2 2025 key).

bullets: 19(2): Freedom Speech; Grounds Sovereignty and integrity, security of State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to an offence
1st Amendment 1951 added public order, friendly relations with foreign States, incitement to an offence and the State-trade clause in 19(6) (LENSD 19 Jun 2026 - the Act's 75th year).

Test: the court decides reasonableness - nature of the right, purpose, extent and urgency of the evil, proportionality (V.G. Row, 1952) ; restrictions must not eclipse the right itself (TH, 23 Feb 2026).
Not a ground under 19(2): sedition, "general public interest", economic grounds . IYB 2026 counts 11 reasonable-restriction heads across Art. 19.

bullets: 32(1): right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings to enforce Part III rights - itself a Fundamental Right.
32(4): right not to be suspended except as the Constitution provides.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar: Art. 32 is "the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it".
Only Fundamental Rights (not statutory or other constitutional rights) are enforced under Art. 32. Its jurisdiction is original but not exclusive.
A right without a remedy is worthless; Art. 32 is itself a Fundamental Right and part of the Basic Structure - cannot be abridged even by amendment (APP; UPSC).

items.title: RBI raises interest rates, hikes FY27 growth forecast by 40 bps and inflation by 20 bps
items.summary: In a notable move, the Reserve Bank of India has adjusted the repo rate, increasing it by 25 basis points to 5.50%. This adjustment comes in response to stronger-than-anticipated economic growth alongside rising price pressures. Additionally, the RBI has updated its FY27 GDP growth prediction to 7.1%, indicating optimistic economic performance.

facts.text: Meanwhile, inflation forecasts have been revised upwards, predicting Consumer Price Index inflation to hover around 5.8%.

bullets: Section 7, RBI Act: after consulting the Governor, the Centre may give RBI directions in the public interest. Consultations under it in 2018 set off the autonomy debate .
The Government appoints the Governor, Deputy Governors and Board, and can supersede the Board (Sec 30) . The MPC and inflation-targeting law (2016) gave RBI operational independence on rates.

bullets: In June 2026, with major central banks gearing up to tighten, the MPC still held at 5.25% and cut its FY27 growth forecast. RBI's inflation forecast assumes crude at $95/barrel, owing to the West Asia conflict (TH, 6 Jun 2026).
Spillover channels: capital outflows, rupee pressure and imported inflation. RBI's special FCNR(B) and forex measures drew about $32 bn after the June policy (TH, 27 Jul 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures › Phillips curve - inflation-unemployment trade-off
bullets: Phillips curve: inverse relation between inflation and unemployment - lower unemployment comes with higher inflation .

India's curve is flat: IIP-CPI data (2012-2026) show little trade-off; ~92% of workers are informal with no wage-bargaining power, so wages do not rise with output (TH, 7 Sep 2026; LENSD, 8 Sep 2026).
Stagflation risk: rate hikes may cut output and jobs without lowering supply-driven inflation.

bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
102nd Amendment let the President notify SEBCs; the 105th Amendment (2021) restored states' power to keep their own lists .

bullets: Women's one-third is a compulsory provision; reservation for backward classes is voluntary (APP; CDI). Reserved seats may be allotted by rotation (APP).
73rd in force 24 April 1993; SC/ST reservation in local bodies lapses with Art. 334 (currently 2030) (CDI).
SC/ST seats at every level are in proportion to population. Chairperson offices are reserved as State law provides and allotted by rotation. States may reserve seats for BCs.

SC/ST reservation (seats and chairpersons) ends with the Art. 334 period, now 2030 under the 104th Amendment (Art. 243D(5)). Women's reservation has no such sunset , so statement 2 in UPPSC 2017 is false.
Backward classes: optional.

items.summary: 07 OCT 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi The fourth UK-India Financial Markets Dialogue (FMD) took place on 29 th September 2026 in London. The Dialogue opened with reflections on developments since the previous meeting in December 2024.

facts.text: Both sides welcomed ongoing regulatory engagement and the role of the India-UK Financial Partnership (IUKFP) in supporting practical cooperation between policymakers, regulators and industry in areas such as Fintech, AI, green and sustainable finance, and asset management.

The UK set out work on the regulatory framework for alternative investment fund managers.

facts.text: He is leading the Indian Delegation at the UNFCCC’s Pre-COP31 meeting being co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu.
The Minister said that the long-term objectives and goals have already been established under the UNFCCC and its Paris Agreement, including the ambition of limiting global temperature rise to 1.5°C.

On Decision-making , Shri Yadav said the key decision required from Parties is to fulfil their commitments under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement “in true letter and spirit” and enable each Party to fulfil these commitments.
On Implementation , the Minister called for addressing identified gaps where the need is highest and the impact is visible and felt by the majority.

items.title: Stark 73% decline in the average size of monitored wildlife populations since 1970, India presents ground for hope: WWF Living Planet Report
items.summary: A global decline of 73% in monitored wildlife populations occurred between 1970 and 2022. India has successfully improved populations of tigers, one-horned rhinos, and Ganga river dolphins. The report highlights threats like habitat loss, climate change, and pollution affecting wildlife. Despite the negative trends, about half of monitored populations are stable or increasing globally.

bullets: IPBES (the "Intergovernmental Panel on Nature"): extinction rates are tens to hundreds of times the natural background rate, and about 25% of assessed plant and animal species are threatened. Habitat destruction is the main driver (UPSC notes).
Living Planet Index is WWF's measure of average change in vertebrate populations since 1970 [GK]. Not in your sources: the latest Living Planet Report figure.
Extinction = death of the last individual of a species, globally or locally (APP).

Recorded losses: IUCN (2014) documented 784 extinctions in 500 years - passenger pigeon, Steller's sea cow (both lost to over-exploitation), Bali, Javan and Caspian tigers (APP). From India: cheetah, pink-headed duck, mountain quail (ZSI via APP).
High-risk traits: large body size, small population, low reproductive rate, narrow/specialised niche, endemism .

bullets: CITES (1973): Mandate Regulate international wildlife trade; Legal status Legally binding on Parties, but does not replace national laws (APP)
CMS / Bonn Convention (1979): Mandate Conservation of migratory species (PYQ 2019); Legal status Binding treaty under UNEP
IUCN (1948): Mandate Red List/Red Data Book; runs thousands of field projects; Legal status Union of governments and NGOs, not a UN organ (APP; UPSC 2015 key: statements 2, 3)
TRAFFIC: Mandate Ensure wildlife trade is not a threat to conservation; Legal status NGO network of WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau (UPSC 2017 key: 2 only)

bullets: IMD's annual Statement on Climate of India: the average yearly temperature in 2020 was 25.78°C (APPSC 2021 key). 2019 was the 7th warmest year since 1901, and Bihar suffered the most (APPSC 2018 key).
India's average temperature rose by about 0.7°C over 1901-2018 (MoES assessment) . (APP says India's rise has "crossed 2°C", which does not match the official series.)
IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum is ≥45°C, whatever the normal maximum (APP). Causes include meandering Rossby waves that create heat domes, and the loo over the Gangetic plains.
AP: heat waves are becoming more frequent and intense in Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur. The hottest place is Rentachintala (Palnadu) (CDI AP Geography, Jul 2026).

Latest: August 2026 total exports $82.7 bn (+25.4%), imports $92.1 bn, deficit $9.4 bn (vs $11.6 bn); merchandise exports +26.1% to $43.8 bn - first time exports grew more than imports in absolute value (TH, 16 Sep 2026). May 2026 goods exports record $45.2 bn (TH, 16 Jun 2026).

Factors widening the deficit since 1991: South-East Asian crisis 1997-98, competition from China, non-tariff barriers of partners, import liberalisation (capital goods, APIs, electronic components), oil and gold. NOT a factor: "lacklustre services" - services did well (PYQ 2017).

bullets: Repo, reverse repo, bank rate: To control inflation (dear money, contractionary) Raise; To boost growth (cheap money, expansionary) Cut
OMO: To control inflation (dear money, contractionary) Sell G-secs; To boost growth (cheap money, expansionary) Buy G-secs
Chain: repo up → money-market rates up → costlier credit → lower consumption and investment → lower aggregate demand → inflation cools (APP).
A CRR/SLR cut raises lendable funds and the money multiplier (M3/M0 = 6.21 on 31 Dec 2025; 6.0 adjusted for SDF) (ES 2025-26).
Raising CRR means less money in circulation and lower demand (APPSC-G1 2022: statements I and II). It does NOT raise purchasing power or banks' lending capacity.

bullets: RBI Governor: How Chairperson (ex officio); casting vote on a tie
6 members, 3 from RBI and 3 from Government (CDI; APP). Decided by majority vote, one vote each (LENS; UPSC).
A statutory body under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, created by the 2016 amendment. It fixes the policy repo rate needed to hit the inflation target, and its decisions bind RBI.
Each member has one vote and decisions are by majority. The Governor has a casting vote in a tie. The MPC must meet at least 4 times a year; in practice it meets bi-monthly (six times).

Latest decisions: on 5 Aug 2026 the MPC voted unanimously to hold the repo at 5.25% with a neutral stance (TH, 6 Aug 2026). The minutes of the August meeting point to a likely hike: headline inflation averaged 3.93% so far this year and core inflation is projected at 4.3% for 2026-27 (TH, 20 Aug 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Monetary policy - objectives, instruments (CRR, SLR, repo, reverse repo, MSF, OMO, LAF), transmission › Evolution of monetary policy since 1991 - phases, challenges, monetary vs fiscal tools
bullets: 1998-2016: Framework Multiple indicator approach (growth, inflation, exchange rate, credit); Landmarks LAF 2000 ; MSS 2004; Base Rate 2010; MSF 2011; MCLR 2016
2016 onwards: Framework Flexible inflation targeting; Landmarks Urjit Patel Committee 2014; MPFA 2015; RBI Act amended 2016; SDF 2022
Authority: Fiscal policy Government (Finance Ministry, Parliament); Monetary policy RBI / MPC
Exchange-rate volatility was a major post-1991 challenge (APPSC 2023 key). Forex reserves were NOT a problem, inflation was not low, and revenue was not in surplus.
Food inflation is mostly supply-driven: rate hikes cannot add onions or tomatoes to the market. It needs fiscal steps too (buffer-stock releases, duty cuts).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures › Phillips curve - inflation-unemployment trade-off
bullets: Phillips curve: inverse relation between inflation and unemployment - lower unemployment comes with higher inflation .

India's curve is flat: IIP-CPI data (2012-2026) show little trade-off; ~92% of workers are informal with no wage-bargaining power, so wages do not rise with output (TH, 7 Sep 2026; LENSD, 8 Sep 2026).
Stagflation risk: rate hikes may cut output and jobs without lowering supply-driven inflation.

The Government appoints the Governor, Deputy Governors and Board, and can supersede the Board (Sec 30) . The MPC and inflation-targeting law (2016) gave RBI operational independence on rates.

bullets: Market intervention (spot and forward), forex reserves, forex swaps, monetary policy signalling (hawkish stance / repo hike attracts carry-trade capital); fiscal policy is not an RBI tool.

Dollar-rupee buy/sell swap: banks sell dollars to RBI and buy them back later at a premium - injects rupee liquidity without permanently altering reserves; $5 billion, 3-year swaps (Dec 2025; another scheduled Apr-May 2026).

bullets: Surplus liquidity speeds up transmission and pulls market rates below the repo. Deficit liquidity weakens it.

sections.topic: Money supply · High-powered money (M0 / reserve money)
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Money supply - M0 to M4, high-powered money, money multiplier, velocity › High-powered money (M0 / reserve money) - components
bullets: Also called reserve money, monetary base, base money, central bank money; basis of credit creation; the most important money indicator for RBI.
As the PYQ frames it: H = currency held by the public + cash reserves of commercial banks (with themselves and with RBI) + other deposits with RBI.
'Other' deposits with RBI: quasi-government and financial institutions (incl. primary dealers), foreign central banks and governments, international agencies such as the IMF.
Uses (components) side: currency held by the public + cash reserves of banks (cash in hand + deposits with RBI) + other deposits with RBI (this is the APPSC-G2 2025 answer).
Money multiplier = M3 / M0. A higher CRR, a higher SLR or a higher currency-deposit ratio (cdr) lowers it. A stronger banking habit raises it (UPSC 2019).

bullets: Base Rate used the average cost of funds, so transmission was slow. MCLR uses the marginal cost of funds: marginal cost of deposits, CRR/SLR carry, operating cost, tenor premium (APP). EBLR links loans to the repo directly, which is the fastest route.
FY26 pass-through: WALR on fresh loans fell 64 bps (ES 2025-26 highlights; CDI's budget note says 69 bps). Credit growth was 14.5% YoY in Dec 2025 (ES).
Accommodative: Meaning Supports growth, ample liquidity, rate cuts likely
Calibrated tightening: Meaning No cuts; hikes measured, not at every meeting
Stance path: neutral to accommodative (Apr 2025), back to neutral (June 2025), neutral retained through Aug 2026 (LENS; ES; TH).

items.title: Additive Manufacturing in India
items.summary: Building India's Future with Next Generation Digital Manufacturing 07 OCT 2026 12:05PM by PIB Delhi India is emerging as a competitive player in digital revolution through Additive Manufacturing (AM), a 3D printing technology in which digital file controls the process of manufacturing. The National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM) is a strategy introduced in 2022 to build India's AM ecosystem.

facts.text: The global AM machines market is projected to touch USD 149 billion by 2035, with the AM-electronics supply chain set to grow from USD 18 billion to USD 112 billion.
This gives India a real opening to become a competitive manufacturer of AM platforms across polymers, metals, composites, ceramics and semiconductor-grade materials.
Slicing : Slicing software divides this digital model into hundreds or thousands of horizontal layers.
Bio Materials: The biomaterials used in AM applications include the hardened material like silicon, calcium phosphate and zinc to support bone structures as new bone growth occurs.

bullets: Three-sector (Clark-Fisher): Author Allan Fisher and Colin Clark; Prediction As income rises, labour and output shift primary → secondary → tertiary

Dual-sector: Author W. Arthur Lewis (1954); Prediction Surplus farm labour (marginal productivity ~zero) moves to the modern industrial sector at a constant wage until the surplus is exhausted - the Lewis turning point
India deviates: output shifted to services while labour stayed on farms, so the Lewis transfer is slow (~46% of workers still in agriculture).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-2 › Trends in India's national income, per capita income and sectoral shares; inter-state GSDP comparison › Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now
bullets: At Independence agriculture was the largest contributor to GDP (APPSC 2023). Industry was about 13% of GDP in 1950-51 (APPSC 2023 key).
Agriculture's share had fallen to about 17% by 2017-18 (APPSC 2019). Services now make up over 50% of GDP, so the order is services > industry > agriculture.
Sector growth, FY 2025-26: agriculture 3.1% (4.6% the year before), industry 6.2%, manufacturing 7.0%, services 9.1% (ES 2025-26; LENS, Jan 2026).
The 2022-23 series raised agriculture's GVA by 3.8-5.9% and cut trade by 36% (TH, 16 Sep 2026).

bullets: Market intervention (spot and forward), forex reserves, forex swaps, monetary policy signalling (hawkish stance / repo hike attracts carry-trade capital); fiscal policy is not an RBI tool.

NRI deposits: RBI bore the full hedging cost on fresh FCNR(B) deposits till 30 Sep 2026; special forex measures mobilised $136.38 billion by 31 Aug 2026 ($127.23 bn via FCNR(B), $5.26 bn OFCBs, $3.89 bn ECBs) (TH, 5 Sep 2026); rupee rose to a two-month high of ₹94.60 on 3 Sep 2026.

Forex reserves: $785.71 billion - India overtook Russia as the 4th largest holder after China, Japan, Switzerland (RBI, LENSD 15 Sep 2026) (earlier: $701.4 bn, Jan 2026, 11 months' import cover, ES 2025-26).
Forex swaps: Example $5 bn, 3-year dollar-rupee buy/sell swap (May 2026) - injects rupee liquidity without permanently cutting reserves

bullets: GDP deflator = Nominal GDP (current prices) / Real GDP (constant prices) x 100 (APPSC-G2 2025).
It is the most comprehensive price measure because it covers all goods and services in GDP (consumption, investment, government, exports), not a fixed basket like CPI/WPI .
GDP deflator = GDP at current prices / GDP at constant prices x 100 - the most comprehensive measure of inflation (covers all final goods and services, not a fixed basket) (G2 2025 key).
Rising deflator = higher price level, lower purchasing power of money ; GNP deflator is the same ratio for GNP .

Dollar-rupee buy/sell swap: banks sell dollars to RBI and buy them back later at a premium - injects rupee liquidity without permanently altering reserves; $5 billion, 3-year swaps (Dec 2025; another scheduled Apr-May 2026).

NRI deposits: RBI bore the full hedging cost on fresh FCNR(B) deposits till 30 Sep 2026; special forex measures mobilised $136.38 billion by 31 Aug 2026 ($127.23 bn via FCNR(B), $5.26 bn OFCBs, $3.89 bn ECBs) (TH, 5 Sep 2026); rupee rose to a two-month high of ₹94.60 on 3 Sep 2026.
Not an RBI exchange-rate tool: fiscal policy adjustments (APPSC-G2 2025 key).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].

Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (in force 2007): 27% OBC seats in central institutions (IYB; GS 2007 key: 93rd Amendment); OBC = classes "so determined by the Central Government" (APP).

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

bullets: Debate: NALSA (2014) asked governments to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward (a vertical OBC-type quota); the community seeks horizontal reservation cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General. The issue resurfaced in June 2023 with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court (APPSC 2022).
Karnataka - first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services (July 2021) (APPSC 2023).

bullets: Qubit can be 0, 1 or any state between (superposition); entanglement links qubits regardless of distance; decoherence (loss of quantum state through the environment) is the main barrier (TH, 9 Jul 2026).
Entanglement sudden death = abrupt total loss of entanglement; Raman Research Institute showed one well-timed local "quantum flip" can delay or prevent it (LENS daily, 16 Sep 2026).
DST quantum-safe report: post-quantum cryptography migration for Critical Information Infrastructure by 2029, others by 2033 (LENS daily, 31 May 2026).

Supremacy machines: Google Sycamore (2019) ; China's photonic Jiuzhang (2020) . Micius (China, 2016) = first quantum communication satellite . Microsoft's Majorana 2 chip raised qubit stability to 20-60 s (APPCA, 2026).
2025 = International Year of Quantum Science and Technology (UN; centenary of quantum mechanics) ; World Quantum Day = 14 April.

sections.topic: Industrial policy · Foreign investment and technology agreements
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Industrial policy - resolutions of 1948, 1956, 1977, 1980 and the New Industrial Policy 1991 › Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit
bullets: New Industrial Policy announced 24 July 1991.

Automatic approval for up to 51% foreign equity in a list of high-priority, high-investment, high-technology industries (e.g. capital goods, entertainment electronics, food processing) - not all industries (APPSC-G1 2012); also for export trading companies.
Automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in high-priority industries; use of foreign brand names/trademarks permitted; Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) set up to speed approvals.
Mandatory convertibility clause (lenders converting loans to equity) was relaxed for term loans; APPSC-G2 2025 key: it applies only to term loans of less than 10 years - learn the key's wording.

Now: FDI up to 100% under the automatic route in most sectors, negative-list approach; FIPB abolished June 2017; approvals via FIF portal, integrated with National Single Window System since Aug 2022 (IYB 2026).

sections.topic: Single Desk Portal and the Single Window Clearance Act
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Approaches and initiatives in AP industry - industrial policy, single desk, MSMEs, industrial nodes › Single Desk Portal and the Single Window Clearance Act - timelines, deemed approval
bullets: The statute is the AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002; 2015 is the launch year of the Single Desk Portal (April 2015). The Act was amended by the AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026, passed Aug 2026 (TH, 20 Aug 2026).

The SDP gives end-to-end processing of 93+ clearances across 19 departments within 21 days. Approvals fall into three categories: self-certification; in-principle approval then inspection; deemed approval if the SLA is breached.
It gives pre-establishment and pre-operation approvals within 21 days (APPSC 2021, 2023). Under IDP 4.0 the portal processes 93+ clearances across 19 departments, still with a 21-day target (CDI).
The AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002 gives the single window statutory force, including deemed approval if a department misses its deadline .

Deemed approval in current practice: the City Gas Distribution policy (G.O. Ms. No. 8, Mar 2026) creates a single window, deemed clearances, a State Level Utilities Coordination Committee under the Chief Secretary, and committees headed by District Collectors (TH, 24 Mar 2026).

sections.topic: Capital-output ratio and savings-investment rate as growth determinants
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-1 › Economic growth vs economic development; measures of development › Capital-output ratio and savings-investment rate as growth determinants
bullets: A higher saving and investment rate raises growth; a higher ICOR (less efficient capital) lowers it .

Capital formation may fail to raise output when capital is idle or badly used, or when complementary inputs are missing: skills, infrastructure, demand. Capital-intensive investment may also add little employment .
